current_episode.title: How to Protect Your Focus, Motivation, & Mental Health: The $17.1 Billion Wake-Up Call

guest.titre: Professor at NYU Stern School of Business
guest.bio_context: Dr. Haidt earned his Ph.D. in social psychology from the University of Pennsylvania. He spent 16 years teaching at the University of Virginia, where he won four teaching awards. He is the author of four New York Times bestsellers, including The Anxious Generation, and is one of the world's leading researchers on how social media and quick dopamine have impacted mental health across generations.

context.real_quote: Intermittent rewards are most effective. Think slot machines.
key_stats: Meta settlement: $17.1 billion in damages due to claims that Facebook and Instagram harmed mental health of kids, teenagers, and adults
Average American teen spends 5 hours per day on social media, mostly watching short videos
2012: Pivotal year when Instagram launches with front-facing camera phones; Facebook buys Instagram this year
2010-2015: The great rewiring of childhood when everyone switched from flip phones to smartphones
2007: iPhone released; very few kids have one initially
15 percent of 14-to-16-year-old teens experience inappropriate approaches from strangers weekly, per research by Arturo Bejar circa 2017-2018
iPhone with front-facing camera introduced in 2010; Instagram launches the same year
entities: New York University Stern School of Business

pending_qa.q: What specific recommendation does research suggest for protecting young people from social media harm?
pending_qa.r: Dr. Haidt's research group states very clearly in The Anxious Generation: no social media till 16. This recommendation stems from research showing that girls need face-to-face connection and genuine friendship, not performing and comparing themselves constantly on platforms designed to maximize engagement and sexualization.
